newsitem.title: USA: "101 Dalmatians" sends Disney earnings higher.
newsitem.headline: "101 Dalmatians" sends Disney earnings higher.

text.p: Strong box office sales for "101 Dalmatians" and record attendance at Walt Disney Co.'s theme parks helped boost its fiscal first quarter profits, the company said on Tuesday.

The Burbank, Calif.-based company said its profits rose 51 percent to $749 million after a gain of $135 million on the sale of Los Angeles television station KCAL. Earnings per share increased 17 percent to $1.09.
The year-ago figures do not include the operations of Capital Cities/ABC, which Disney acquired in February in a $19 billion deal.

Walt Disney World and its resorts in Florida posted record attendance as tourists flocked to the park to celebrate its 25th anniversary, the company said. Revenue from Disney theme parks and resorts rose 16 percent to $1.2 billion for the quarter.

Results also reflected the opening of Disney's largest retail store in the world, which sells everything from cartoon-shaped pasta to expensive evening bags with Mickey Mouse ears. The store is near Walt Disney World in Florida.

Disney credited its re-make of "101 Dalmatians," the international release of "the Hunchback of Notre Dame," and other movies such as "The English Patient" with contributing to the quarter's strong performance.

"Walt Disney World led the way in our theme park division and the impressive box office performance of our holiday movies and home video releases also contributed to the company's results," said Michael Eisner, Disney chairman. "Worldwide merchandise licensing and ESPN continue to show strong growth and were significant factors in the company's overall performance."

Disney also said it would begin reviewing its options for the publishing operations it acquired as part of the ABC acquisition. The unit includes the printing and distribution of daily and weekly newspapers, specialised publications for various industries, and consumer, special interest and agricultural publications.
On Monday, Disney announced it would increase its quarterly dividend to 13 cents per share from 11 cents.
